blocks.text: LIMA, Peru — Scientists have discovered a new species of lizard in the Peruvian Andes, the Natural History Museum of San Marcos University said Saturday. The lizard measures between six and eight centimeters (2.4-3.2 inches) and has distinct coloration depending on sex. Females have square-shaped spots on their backs, while males have oblique spots and white scales that help them blend into their rocky surroundings. READ: Fujimori takes charge in Peru amid China, US balancing act The lizard feeds on plants and small arthropods, including spiders, beetles, true bugs and insect larvae.
